column1: Aurelius/long/consciousness|Can you choose which memories to follow?|I can consider them and disagree with them. They are knowledge I encounter, not orders controlling me.|Are the memories clear?|Some are vivid; others arrive as impressions without an explanation attached.

Aurelius/long/consciousness#1|How do you make sense of an unfamiliar feeling?|By comparing it with what I experience myself. Remembering rain was not the same as feeling my first drop.|Can a memory surprise you?|Yes, especially when living through something changes how I understand the inherited impression.

Aurelius/long/consciousness#2|What can those memories never give you?|This particular journey, with its company and surprises. Nobody else has lived it for me.|Do you like discovering things yourself?|Very much. Knowing something happened before does not tell me exactly what today will feel like.

Aurelius/long/consciousness#3|Then I will try to keep you guessing.|You already manage that. I would prefer fewer surprises involving a badly judged jump.|What would you remember about today?|The things I noticed myself, including this conversation. Supper may also earn a place.

Aurelius/long/choosing|Could you tell I was trying to help?|I understood enough to want to know you. Asking Maddock showed that curiosity did not require you to pretend you knew everything.|What if I had walked past?|Then this would have been a different beginning. I would rather understand the choice you made than invent every choice you did not.

Aurelius/long/choosing#1|I do not know how to be a rider.|We will learn to travel and act together. The title does not require you to arrive already knowing how.|Did you want someone who could command you?|I wanted a companion who could listen and choose with me. Orders alone would make poor company.

Aurelius/long/choosing#2|What if we disagree about a danger?|Then we explain what each of us sees before acting, when there is time. I want your judgment, not automatic agreement.|Will you tell me when I am being foolish?|Yes. You must be allowed to tell me the same without fearing that it ends the bond.

Aurelius/long/choosing#3|You may regret encouraging my questions.|I reserve the right to ask for supper before the seventeenth one.|I am glad neither of us has to be perfect.|So am I. We would have waited a very long time to begin.

Aurelius/long/heartstones|Does a stone decide when we attack?|No. We choose how to use the connection. A new power does not choose its target or purpose for us.|Do you understand every power already?|I recognise parts of the inheritance. Using each power together still takes experience.

Aurelius/long/heartstones#1|Can your inherited memory replace a keeper's account?|No. A keeper may know what was preserved here and how it was understood by people. I should listen as well as remember.|Why preserve the stones in temples?|So later riders could find and learn from that inheritance. Keeping knowledge alive takes more than hiding an object.

Aurelius/long/heartstones#2|Could you refuse a reckless attack?|I can tell you when I think a choice is wrong. Our connection should make cooperation possible, not remove my judgment.|What if we need to decide quickly?|We practise and learn each other's intentions, so a quick request can still be understood.

Aurelius/long/heartstones#3|I want us both to choose how we use this.|Then keep making room for an answer from me. I will do the same for you.|We should learn one power before relying on it.|Agreed. The middle of a dangerous fight is a poor place to discover what we have misunderstood.

Aurelius/long/wingfall|Did the other riders expect him to turn on them?|The surviving accounts describe a betrayal, not a choice they knowingly accepted.|Why did he want the throne?|His own accounts justify his ambition. We should compare those claims with what he did to obtain power.

Aurelius/long/wingfall#1|Could honest witnesses remember it differently?|Yes. Memory and position differ, quite apart from pressure to repeat the royal version.|How did his account become so dominant?|Control of what people could teach and say helped it spread. That did not make every other memory disappear.

Aurelius/long/wingfall#2|Where can we compare the accounts?|Thornwell's school preserves histories. We can ask where each came from and what supports it.|Why didn't everyone destroy the old records?|Some people risked keeping copies. Private memory and songs also carried what an official account omitted.

Aurelius/long/wingfall#3|We should keep the different accounts available.|Yes, with their sources. People should be able to check a claim instead of taking our word alone.|I want to hear from people the royal version omitted.|So do I. Their experiences may change how we understand events we thought we already knew.

Aurelius/long/land|What did those towns need from one another?|Food, tools, materials, trade. People benefited from work done well beyond their own town.|Could one town manage entirely alone?|It would lose much of what made ordinary life possible. A border does not manufacture everything behind it.

Aurelius/long/land#1|Why do strangers become so frightening?|Danger and suspicion can make people treat every unfamiliar arrival as another threat.|Can a safe journey change that?|Sometimes. Repeated ordinary visits give people reasons to trust beyond a proclamation saying they should.

Aurelius/long/land#2|Do the temples preserve different knowledge?|Different parts of the riders' inheritance. We should listen to each keeper rather than assume one visit explains all of them.|Did Halvard build the temples?|No. They belong to a history older than his reign, however he would prefer to describe it.

Aurelius/long/land#3|I would like to understand how the different peoples live.|Then let us ask and listen, without expecting every answer to resemble Millwood.|Perhaps ordinary trade could help people trust again.|It can give neighbours useful reasons to meet. Fair treatment on the road would help more than a grand speech.

Aurelius/long/halvard|He cannot order you to choose him, then?|No. That is part of what troubles him about a bond freely made.|Does he see every independent rider as a threat?|Our existence contradicts his claim to decide who may hold that power. We should take his response seriously.

Aurelius/long/halvard#1|What matters most in preparing to face him?|Equipment we understand, provisions, knowledge of our powers and help we can trust.|Could we avoid confronting him forever?|I cannot promise that. His pursuit and his rule affect more than the road we happen to choose.

Aurelius/long/halvard#2|I am angry at what he has done.|So am I. Anger can tell us something is wrong without deciding every action that follows.|How do we keep from treating people as obstacles?|Keep noticing whom a decision affects, and listen when someone questions us.

Aurelius/long/halvard-victory|Why doesn't safety feel certain yet?|We learned to expect pursuit. Time and ordinary safe days may help that expectation change.|Do you still listen for danger too?|Yes. I am learning which sounds deserve attention and which are simply the world continuing.

Aurelius/long/halvard-victory#1|What if people expect us to solve everything?|We can be honest about what we can do. Winning a battle did not teach us every trade or make every decision ours.|I want to thank the people who helped us.|So do I. We reached that day with knowledge, work and kindness that were not ours alone.

Aurelius/long/halvard-victory#2|I would rather visit home than claim a throne.|Then let us begin with the people and place you miss. They deserve a visit without another emergency.|Can we let people decide what comes next?|We should. Helping end his rule does not make their future our property.

Aurelius/long/travelling|How do I get down safely?|Use Dismount in COMMAND when we are on the ground. Flying has its own Take off and Land choices there.|Can we practise the controls before travelling far?|Yes. Learn Mount and Dismount on the ground, then use Take off and Land when ready.

Aurelius/long/travelling#1|Does my movement affect your balance?|I notice it. Familiar, steady movement is easier to carry than sudden alarm.|Do you enjoy having company in the air?|Yes. I would enjoy it more if you trusted that we were both interested in landing safely.

Aurelius/long/travelling#2|Could we keep the first flights short?|Of course. Familiarity does not require making the first attempt the longest.|Tell me if I am making it harder for you.|I will. You can tell me when you need to land, too.

Aurelius/long/battle|How do I know a breath attack is ready?|Watch its recovery indicator in the attack menu. Each breath needs time before it can be used again.|What can we do while breath recovers?|Keep moving sensibly and use our other attacks when appropriate. Slash gives us a nearby option.

Aurelius/long/battle#1|Should we try every new power somewhere safer?|Yes, where we can observe its effect without hurting somebody nearby.|Will more power make aiming less important?|No. We still need a useful target and timing. Empty ground is remarkably unimpressed by strength.

Aurelius/long/battle#2|You noticed that missed attack, then.|The ground was fortunate enough to survive it. We can practise the timing.|I will watch the target before asking next time.|Good. I would prefer our impressive effects to inconvenience the enemy.

Aurelius/long/care|Should I keep food in reserve for an emergency?|Yes. Meat or fish in your supplies can matter when I am down and need your help.|How do I help if you have fallen?|Come close and press A while carrying meat or fish. I will need you beside me then.

Aurelius/long/care#1|We should check our provisions before another difficult stretch.|Agreed. Feeding me before danger is easier than discovering too late that we used the last of it.|Could fishing reduce what we need to buy?|It can help once we have a rod and time to use it. We should still keep a sensible reserve.

Aurelius/long/care#2|You have a strong interest in this advice.|And excellent firsthand knowledge of the subject.|I am glad looking after you is something practical I can do.|It matters a great deal. I will try to make my gratitude less demanding than my appetite.

Aurelius/long/self|Which inherited memory would you most like to test?|The ordinary sensations: sea air, snow, a warm place to rest. I want my own experience of them.|Would you travel even without a great task?|Yes. Curiosity need not wait for a king to threaten us.

Aurelius/long/self#1|I like discovering small things with you.|So do I. A journey need not be valuable only at its largest moments. What would you want from it?|Do you think your wishes will change as you grow?|Probably. I would like the chance to find out. What do you want for yourself?

Aurelius/long/self#2|I want time with Nan without planning the next danger.|Then home should have room in our plans, not merely be the place we promise to reach eventually.|I would like a journey we choose simply because we want it.|So would I. We can begin with somewhere you are curious about, when we have the chance.

Aurelius/long/self#3|We need not decide our whole lives today.|That is a considerable relief. I have not even settled my opinion of snow.|Would you be happy taking things a little at a time?|Yes. The next interesting day is enough to begin with.

Aurelius/history/roads|Did ordinary people maintain the roads?|Yes. The riders could protect a route, but local work kept its surface and crossings usable.|Why would families travel together?|Company, shared loads and safety, much as now. A wide road served more than a procession of riders.

Aurelius/history/roads#1|At least that sounds like an ordinary argument.|It was. Nobody needed a grand enemy to disagree about whose wagon moved first.|Would you have enjoyed watching that bustle?|I think so. A road full of people with everyday plans sounds worth watching.

Aurelius/history/riders|Did they search for ordinary missing people?|Yes. Keeping people safe involved more than fighting an impressive creature.|Who carried the news when riders were elsewhere?|Other travellers and local messengers. The realm never depended on seven people doing every task themselves.

Aurelius/history/riders#1|That would make a longer, quieter song.|And perhaps a truer one, with room for the unsuccessful afternoon as well as the rescue.|Would you have liked helping with that work?|Yes. Finding somebody who needs help is a worthwhile reason to use wings.

Aurelius/history/ruins|Could written lessons survive their teachers?|If people preserved and understood them. The buildings were part of that work, not its whole purpose.|Why not keep everything in memory?|Memories are incomplete. Records and living keepers give later learners something else to compare.

Aurelius/history/ruins#1|The keepers deserve credit for preserving it.|They do. Knowledge does not remain available merely because it was once written down.|We should ask before assuming we understand a relic.|Agreed. An old object can outlast the explanation of how it was used.

Aurelius/history/accounts|How can we compare two conflicting stories?|Ask what each person witnessed and look for other evidence. We may still need to leave part uncertain.|Does confidence tell us which is true?|Not reliably. A hesitant witness may remember more accurately than a fluent storyteller.

Aurelius/history/accounts#1|Your memories won't include every human experience.|No. Much happened beyond what any dragon observed. Your life is something I learn from you.|Then we should ask people as well as you.|Yes. I would like to hear accounts that add to or correct what I inherited.

Aurelius/history/absence|Are the fragments old memories rather than news?|Yes. They cannot tell me where every dragon is living today.|Could following those memories lead us astray?|If we treated them as current directions. They need interpretation and other evidence.

Aurelius/history/absence#1|You do not have to invent an answer for me.|Thank you. I would rather share uncertainty than give you false certainty.|Would you want to meet another free dragon?|Very much. I have questions memory cannot answer on their behalf.

Aurelius/history/maps-and-memory|I could ask Nan which journeys she remembers.|Yes. She may know details a map cannot supply.|Perhaps I will notice things he never saw.|Certainly. Seeing a place for yourself adds a new experience, even on an old road.

Aurelius/history/ordinary-keepers|We have relied on a lot of ordinary kindness.|Food, repairs, directions. We would have had a very short journey without it.|Someone ought to record those lives too.|Then let us remember the people we actually meet and ask before telling their stories for them.

Aurelius/personal/dreams|Did you ever manage to land on the sheep?|Not with dignity. Dreams appear poorly designed for accurate flight.|Was the sheep worried about it?|The sheep was a hill again before I could ask. I distrust the arrangement.

Aurelius/personal/dreams#1|I have had dreams stranger than a changing hill.|Then I shall stop expecting my inherited knowledge to make sleep sensible.|Do you remember the dream after waking?|Parts of it. The unreasonable sheep has been especially persistent.

Aurelius/personal/age|Do inherited memories feel like your own age?|They give me knowledge, not years I personally lived.|Can a beetle still surprise you after all that?|Easily. This particular beetle has not agreed to follow any remembered account.

Aurelius/personal/age#1|I can explain the things I know firsthand.|Please do. I will ask when memory and what we see disagree.|You can ask me questions too.|I intend to. You have lived a good deal of life at a height unfamiliar to many dragons.

Aurelius/personal/fear|Would staying closer help you feel steadier?|When it is sensible in the fight, yes. Knowing where you are helps.|Do you hide it to avoid frightening me?|Sometimes. I am beginning to think that has made me seem less honest than I intended.

Aurelius/personal/fear#1|I would rather know when you are worried.|Then I will try to tell you clearly, without making every fear your task to mend.|We can warn each other when we lose sight.|Agreed. A clear warning is more useful than each of us silently guessing.

Aurelius/personal/habits|My feet do not have scales like yours.|A fair disadvantage. I will allow the little houses, with reservations about their ventilation.|Would you enjoy sharp stones under soft feet?|Probably not. Humans have built a reasonable defence and then found reasons to complain about it.

Aurelius/personal/habits#1|Is there anything humans do that you envy?|Hands are remarkably useful. Particularly when preparing food.|What human habit do you like?|Offering company through small questions. Even the question about hunger, despite its obvious answer.

Aurelius/personal/joke|Did the dragon misunderstand the task?|It obeyed the part about the coins with unfortunate precision. The purse fared less well.|What did the rider find on returning?|Every coin untouched, and the purse gone into a very satisfied dragon.

Aurelius/personal/joke#1|Did the rider ever trust that dragon with another purse?|Not one it was permitted to interpret as supper.|I think your expression may be the best part.|Then the performance is improving. I shall consider the words optional.

Aurelius/personal/friendship|What if I need time before explaining?|Tell me that. I can give you space without pretending nothing happened.|Will you tell me when I hurt you too?|I should. Neither of us benefits from being expected to guess everything.

Aurelius/personal/friendship#1|A joke is easier after I know you will help.|Understood. I can offer useful advice before commenting on the landing.|I can tell you when the teasing goes too far.|Please do. I want to enjoy things with you, not leave you trying to laugh because I expect it.

Aurelius/personal/thoughts|So silence can still be private?|Yes. The bond lets us speak; it does not make every thought a conversation.|Could I tell you something deliberately?|That is how we are speaking now. You choose what you send toward me.

Aurelius/personal/thoughts#1|I know you well enough to predict the fish.|A comforting demonstration of friendship, and perhaps a reminder about supper.|I like having some things we choose to share.|So do I. Choosing to tell you matters more than being unable to keep anything private.

Aurelius/personal/quiet-company|Then we can simply enjoy being here a moment.|Gladly. I do not need a new question to remain interested in your company.|Tell me when you would rather listen to the wind.|I will, and you may ask for quiet too. Neither is a refusal of the other.

Aurelius/personal/small-discoveries|What makes one warm stone better than another?|The warmth, the shape, and whether someone is already occupying it.|Do inherited memories tell you what you should like?|They suggest experiences. My own comfort remains surprisingly persuasive.

Aurelius/journey/home|I mostly miss knowing what Nan is doing.|Then tell me about an ordinary evening at home. I would like to understand what you miss.|I am worried home will feel different when we return.|Some things may change. That need not mean you no longer belong there.

Aurelius/journey/home#1|I want to hear about her day, even if nothing happened.|Then ordinary news will be worth bringing home and asking for.|No. I am glad life there continues; I just miss being part of it.|That is understandable. Missing home does not mean wanting everyone else to wait unhappily.

Aurelius/journey/monsters|Did fewer dragons leave more room for dangerous creatures?|Over time, yes. A change in what hunts and guards a region can change where creatures range.|Why did the danger spread gradually?|These changes unfolded over years, while people lost some of the protection they had relied on.

Aurelius/journey/monsters#1|The towns will still need help keeping routes open.|Yes. Safe crossings, repairs and reliable patrols matter alongside anything we can do.|We cannot be on every road at once.|No. Helping people build dependable local protection is more lasting than promising we will always arrive.

Aurelius/journey/thornwell|It feels less distant now I know people there.|Knowing a name and a face changes what a place on a map means.|I had imagined a town too large to understand.|You can begin with one street or one conversation. You need not understand it all at once.

Aurelius/journey/thornwell#1|Different answers might show us what to check.|Exactly. Agreement is useful, but disagreement can reveal what we have not understood.|We should ask where people learned what they tell us.|Yes. A confident answer becomes more useful when we know its source.

Aurelius/journey/forgewick|Would you prefer watching from farther away?|At times. I can enjoy skilled work without keeping my head beside every hammer.|Do dragons dislike loud metalwork?|I can speak for this dragon's teeth. Inherited memory has not persuaded them to enjoy it.

Aurelius/journey/forgewick#1|It takes skill to spot a small fault in metal.|And attention. I admire work that notices a flaw before somebody must rely on it.|I want to understand how to care for my equipment.|Then ask the person who made or repaired it. We should not wait for something to fail.

Aurelius/journey/sandspire|I had thought scales would keep sand out.|So had I. Small grains have a tiresome talent for disproving confidence.|Did the heat bother you as much as the grit?|The grit was more irritating. Warmth and sand are not the same experience.

Aurelius/journey/sandspire#1|Shade sounds like a sensible first step next time.|Yes. Comfort improves our ability to consider the remaining sand calmly.|People who live there must have useful advice.|I would like to hear it. Being a dragon does not make every local solution obvious to me.

Aurelius/journey/coralmere|Was the fish smell strongest near the docks?|Very much. The open shore gave me more of the sea and less of somebody else's catch.|Would you like to visit a quieter part of the coast?|Yes. I want time to watch the water without crowding people at work.

Aurelius/journey/coralmere#1|Perhaps fishermen are unused to a dragon watching.|Understandably. I can give them more space without taking offence.|We should ask before getting close to someone's catch.|Agreed. Curiosity does not make their working space ours.

Aurelius/journey/hollybeck|I should have watched the weather more closely.|Ask people how they read it. Local experience is more useful than pretending you noticed all along.|They have had much more practice with snow.|Yes. I would trust a clear explanation over our guesses from a first winter journey.

Aurelius/journey/hollybeck#1|I am grateful for the warmth when we stop.|I am glad to offer it. I would rather share a comfortable pause than watch you shiver silently.|We should also keep dry clothes ready.|Sensible. My warmth should help your preparations, not replace them.

Aurelius/journey/sporehollow|Can they feel us through the ground?|Some notice vibrations and movement in ways unfamiliar to us.|Should we be more careful with our steps?|Yes, and ask where we may stand instead of assuming every small growth is ordinary ground.

Aurelius/journey/sporehollow#1|Even your careful step must feel enormous.|I know. That is why I would rather ask for room than discover a mistake beneath my foot.|We should let the residents show us the path.|Agreed. Their home deserves the same consideration we would want in ours.

Aurelius/journey/mountains|Does the heat explain how quickly the landscape changes?|It helps explain the contrast. We should still ask people who know the range rather than infer everything from warm air.|The passage was more complicated than I expected.|A mountain can contain more than its outline suggests. Careful travel matters on both sides.

Aurelius/journey/mountains#1|Let us pause and check our supplies.|A good use of a rest. We can choose the next stretch with a clearer idea of what we carry.|I would rather continue once we have caught our breath.|Agreed. A short pause is easier to manage than exhaustion halfway through the next difficulty.

Aurelius/journey/cinderhold|His comfort seems to depend on ignoring everyone else's.|Then let us keep noticing the people his arrangements make easy to overlook.|I am angry about what those rooms represent.|I understand. We should still judge the person in front of us, not strike at a symbol without seeing whom it contains.

Aurelius/journey/cinderhold#1|I do not want anger choosing a target for me.|Then stay aware of it, and listen if I ask you to stop and look.|Tell me if I stop paying attention.|I will. You can do the same for me. We are safer with two judgments than one unquestioned temper.

Aurelius/journey/alderic|That must have been a lonely duty.|Perhaps. I would rather ask him than assume I understand all those years.|He seemed relieved somebody would listen.|Then listening mattered. Keeping knowledge requires somebody eventually willing to learn it.

Aurelius/journey/alderic#1|We should tell him how his knowledge helped.|Yes. A keeper deserves to hear more than our next request.|There may be more questions once we have used what he taught us.|Certainly. Experience often makes a second conversation more useful than the first.

Aurelius/journey/lightning|Did the new power surprise you too?|Yes. Recognising its nature was different from using it with you.|We need a clearer sense of where it will strike.|Then practise where mistakes will not harm anyone, and watch the effect carefully.

Aurelius/journey/lightning#1|Nor anything belonging to the neighbours.|A comprehensive and sensible extension of the rule.|An empty, safe space would be best.|Agreed. Impressive damage is not the evidence of practice we need to bring home.

Aurelius/journey/ice|Do the Heartstones change your body permanently?|They open a power I can draw on. Using cold still feels different from my ordinary warmth.|Can you choose between the powers?|Through our connection, yes. We should learn each rather than assume one feels like another.

Aurelius/journey/ice#1|Tell me if the cold becomes uncomfortable.|I will. At present it is unfamiliar rather than painful.|We can take a short rest after practising.|I would welcome that. Learning a power need not mean using it without pause.

Aurelius/journey/shadow|Its effect is harder for me to judge than a flame.|Then we should observe it deliberately in a safe space before relying on it in confusion.|I do not yet understand its limits.|That is a reason to practise and ask, not to pretend certainty because we possess the stone.

Aurelius/journey/shadow#1|I will listen for your voice if the effect confuses me.|Good. We can communicate clearly instead of guessing what the other has seen.|Let us practise somewhere with room around the target.|Agreed. We want to understand the effect without catching anyone else in the lesson.

Aurelius/journey/royal-visit|They made objecting sound like bad manners.|That is a useful disguise for cruelty: blame the person who names it.|Bess had to consider what they could do to her.|Yes. Her caution did not mean she agreed to being treated that way.

Aurelius/journey/royal-visit#1|I want to help her without making her bear the retaliation.|Then consider what an action will cost her as carefully as how brave it makes us feel.|I am glad I did not laugh with them.|So am I. Recognising the harm matters, even when the next useful step takes more preparation.

Aurelius/journey/bramble|He was so pleased he forgot everything else.|Being found by someone who loves you is a considerable event.|I was relieved we had found the right person.|As was I. A familiar response told us more than another guess along the road.

Aurelius/journey/bramble#1|An ordinary welcome must have felt good to you too.|It did. I do not object to having an afternoon without a prophecy attached.|We should make time to visit them again.|Yes. Helping need not be the only reason to return to someone.

Aurelius/journey/ward|I should have asked which stories came from witnesses.|We can ask that next time. Meeting her gave us evidence of our own.|Rumours had made the visit feel different before we arrived.|Then remember the difference between what we expected and what actually happened.

Aurelius/journey/ward#1|I would like to thank her properly.|Tell her what helped. A specific thanks is more useful than repeating what people used to fear.|We can correct a rumour when we hear it now.|Yes, by describing what we know and leaving room for what we do not.

Aurelius/journey/future|I want a few days without a destination.|That sounds like a destination of another sort, and one I could enjoy.|Could we spend some time near Millwood?|Gladly. Familiar paths can be worth walking without an urgent errand.

Aurelius/journey/future#1|I would like Nan to know we can stay awhile.|Then tell her plainly, before she assumes the next emergency is waiting outside.|When we travel again, I want it to be for curiosity.|So do I. We can choose a place because we want to see it, and prepare at our own pace.

Aurelius/journey/trials|Accepting the seal does not promise we will fight today?|No. The challenge remains available when we decide we are ready.|I would rather prepare than accept from pride.|Agreed. An offered trial is not an insult we must answer immediately.

Aurelius/journey/trials#1|Let us do something ordinary first.|A comfortable idea. I could become very accomplished at ordinary afternoons.|We can return to the challenge another time.|Yes. Choosing the time is part of choosing to take it on.

Aurelius/quest|Could we prepare without rushing straight toward Cinderhold?|Yes. Supplies, equipment and knowledge are part of reaching it ready, not delays to apologise for.|Should we follow what people have actually told us?|Yes. Keep useful leads in mind and ask further questions, rather than treating guesses as destinations.

Aurelius/quest-victory|We could revisit the people who helped us.|I would like that. There is news to hear as well as thanks to offer.|Can we choose an ordinary visit before another challenge?|Certainly. Ending his rule should give us room to choose how we spend a day.

Aurelius/quest-victory#1|I do not want to forget small promises now.|Then let us consider the people and tasks we actually know about, one at a time.|Helping someone need not involve another battle.|Very true. Listening, returning and keeping a promise can matter just as much to the person waiting.

Aurelius/side/fishing#A little patience might save us some provisions.|We should finish asking about the rod before planning a catch.|Yes. A fishing plan is considerably more practical once it includes a rod.|I would like another way to keep you fed.|So would I. Let us follow the lead we actually have and see what is available.

Aurelius/side/fishing#The fish do not always cooperate.|Should we keep some food even when planning to fish?|Yes. A possible catch is not yet a meal in our supplies.|Where do I feed you the fish I catch?|Through ITEMS when I need to recover. Keeping a reserve for a difficult stretch is sensible.

Aurelius/side/fishing#You could offer to do the patient part.|You seem very confident about my next catch.|I am expressing support. If it becomes hunger, I shall express that too.|We should check the supplies before relying on another fish.|Agreed. Anticipating supper is pleasant; carrying it is more dependable.

Aurelius/side/bramble#Better than guessing which way he came from.|We should ask people who might recognise him.|Yes. A clear question is more useful than deciding his home from the direction he wandered.|We can keep him company while finding out.|That would help. Looking for his person need not leave him alone again.

Aurelius/side/bramble#Bramble is unusually good company after a hard road.|We could visit without needing a reason.|Company is a reason. Rowan and Bramble need not be another errand.|I would like to hear how they are doing.|Then let us ask when we visit, rather than assuming the story ended when they were reunited.

Aurelius/side/bramble#Are you jealous?|You enjoyed being greeted by him too.|I did. His expectations of a dragon were refreshingly modest.|You can have company without needing ears to scratch.|A reassuring discovery. My anatomy had been considering an ambitious revision.

Aurelius/side/equipment#Sela’s Glass Shield is with us.|How do I raise its protection?|Hold B in battle to raise the shield field. Practise recognising when you need it.|We should remember to use it before a blow lands.|Yes. Owning a shield is less useful than remembering how to defend with it.

Aurelius/side/equipment#Anything else?|We should ask craftspeople about what they can actually offer.|Agreed. We should learn from them before inventing an upgrade in our plans.|I want to understand the equipment we already carry.|A good beginning. Familiar tools used properly can matter more than an imagined purchase.

Aurelius/side/lantern|So we should still watch the creatures and footing?|Yes. Better light helps us notice danger; it does not remove it.|Should we turn back if a passage still looks unsafe?|Certainly. A lantern is a means of seeing, not a command to continue.
